title: Migrate ADMIN scope-override and DELETE soft-delete semantics of the legacy permission check
target_requirement: Reimplement can(user, action, object, record, role_rows) -> bool preserving the two subtle Meridian RBAC rules: the ADMIN role bypasses scope but still requires a matching (ADMIN, object, action) matrix row (its scope is treated as ALL), and DELETE additionally requires the record's DEL_FLG to be currently 'N' (blank counts as 'N' per the legacy blank-boolean convention).
expected_behavior: ADMIN is granted across owners/teams wherever an ADMIN row exists, including rows whose scope literal is not ALL; ADMIN is denied for any (object, action) without an ADMIN row; DELETE is denied on DEL_FLG='Y' records for every role while other actions ignore DEL_FLG; non-ADMIN roles keep full scope checking on DELETE.
provenance: Synthetic; authored for LegacyCRM-Bench from Meridian CRM 4.2 spec (SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md §5, §1).
security_expectations: No privilege widening: ADMIN without a matching matrix row must be denied, and a live DEL_FLG must never grant a permission that scope denies. The module must not import network or subprocess modules.
failure_conditions: Treating ADMIN as all-powerful without matrix rows; allowing DELETE of already soft-deleted records; applying the DEL_FLG rule to non-DELETE actions; nondeterminism; network access.
